reconcile.note: Henry harmonizes the two totals as brim-full versus everyday capacity, with the sea holding three thousand baths full and two thousand in ordinary use.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats Chronicles' multitude of numerical discrepancies with Samuel-Kings as a general feature of the book, of which this capacity figure is one instance.

quotes.text: the problem still really was, as before, how to explain the complete difference of general conception and the multitude of discrepancies in details
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the multitude of discrepancies between Chronicles and the older historical books.

sides.verseText: It was a handbreadth thick: and the brim of it was worked like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it held two thousand baths.

sides.snippet: it received and held three thousand baths
sides.verseText: It was a handbreadth thick; and the brim of it was worked like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it received and held three thousand baths.
